title: Spiced parsnip and red lentil pot

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or a fine staple: vegetable stock, tinned tomatoes, red lentils and natural yoghurt.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday Tesco item at an ordinary price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs one large pan and a wooden spoon, and the technique is simple softening and simmering.

works.reason: 200g red lentils and 500g parsnips in a litre of stock plus a tin of tomatoes give a thick, well-seasoned pot for four, and small parsnip cubes will be tender in 20 minutes.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes covers peeling and cubing the parsnips, chopping the onion and shredding the kale, and the 25 minute cook matches 5 minutes of softening plus a 20 minute simmer.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the lemon, is used in the steps, the names match their ids and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm spiced parsnip and lentil pot suits early October, and the parsnips are the bulk and point of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling meal of vegetables and pulses with a yoghurt topping that a family would happily eat again.
